scope: Align the bilingual Larry detail page with the released Steam edition; no game files, saves, legal pages, guide step translations or build outputs changed.

findings.claim: The player is Larry, the bar owner. The game is a single-player text adventure, not a premise about getting to know Larry as a separate romantic lead.
evidence: officialSnapshot.detailed_description: player role, locations and dialogue choices
steam/content/game/data/lang/en.js: ui About the Game text

findings.claim: The current English product title is Larry's Mixology Lab.
evidence: steam/content/game/data/lang/en.js: ui[賴瑞的調酒研究室]

findings.claim: Title-screen and toolbar instructions use the shipped UI labels, including Restart, Quick Save, Quick Load, Save Slots, Load Game and Endings.
There are 40 numbered local save slots, with a separate quick-save/load flow. No claim is made that 40 slots cover every choice or remove the need to restart.
evidence: officialSnapshot.detailed_description: 40 local slots and quick save/load

findings.claim: Completed endings are recorded automatically only after the ending finishes and exits to the post-ending section. Unreached ending names stay hidden.
Steam controls include click, Enter or Space to advance; F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen and Esc leaves it. Settings offers text-size controls and the tutorial.
evidence: steam/content/game/data/lang/en.js: Keyboard Controls and Settings labels

findings.claim: Eight game languages are supported and the game has no character voice acting. Website-language count is not substituted for game-language support.
evidence: officialSnapshot.detailed_description: eight interface/script languages and no character voices

removedOrCorrected: Replaced the old iOS description and screenshot-only source attribution with Steam release and local-source evidence.
Corrected the player-role and English-title mismatch; removed unsupported otome/romantic-companion positioning.
Replaced the outdated title-screen-only save/load instructions with current Steam toolbar and save-panel labels.
Removed the guarantee that 40 slots can hold every important choice and that players never need to start over.
Used qualified language for choice effects and practical instructions instead of unsupported promotional claims.
